title: DR1 asks the four questions that the reason for import opens inline, as reveals under the reason the user picks; the frontend asks them on four pages of their own reached through a separate hub task.

finding.frontend: The frontend asks the main reason on its own page and then, depending on the answer, sends the user on to as many as three further pages, each with its own heading, its own Save and continue and its own return to the hub. Internal market leads to 'Purpose in the internal market'. Transhipment or onward travel leads to 'Destination country'. Transit leads to 'Destination country' and then 'Port of exit', in that order. Temporary admission horses leads to 'Port of exit' and 'Exit date'. Reason and purpose sit in one hub task and the other three sit in a second, conditional task called Exit details (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:34-39). A user answering for transit therefore visits three pages and crosses two hub tasks to answer one question and its consequences.
finding.prototype: DR1 asks all of it on one page. The radio group on 'Main reason for import' carries a conditional reveal under four of its five options (app/routes.js:8778-8820), and the questions appear in place the moment the radio is chosen: Internal market reveals the eleven-option 'Purpose in the internal market' radio group; Transhipment or onward travel reveals a Destination country select; Transit reveals Port of exit and then Destination country, in that order; Temporary admission horses reveals an Exit date picker and then a Port of exit select. Re-entry reveals nothing. One page, one Save and continue, one hub task. Every reveal is present in the rendered page and hidden until its radio is chosen, which is why the captured temporary-admission state carries all six reveal fields in its DOM.
finding.difference: Move the four follow-up questions onto the reason page as govukRadios conditional reveals and retire the four separate pages, in reveal order per reason: purpose under Internal market; destination country under Transhipment; port of exit then destination country under Transit; exit date then port of exit under Temporary admission horses. Both the transit pair and the temporary-admission pair come out in the reverse of the frontend's page order today. One consequence follows: the Exit details hub task disappears, and with it the trap where that task renders as a visible unlinked row under Temporary admission horses because its gate tests only the first of its three pages. DR1 has no equivalent trap because it has no second row to gate, so a reason that opens only exit date and port of exit cannot produce a dead row. That hub change is owned by the hub slice and depends on this one. Answers do not need a separate decision: both sides drop a reveal answer once its reason is no longer chosen, so nothing changes about what survives a flip.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding that DR1 routes away from /reason-for-import to a separate page for any of purpose, destination country, port of exit or exit date, rather than rendering it in the conditional block on the reason page itself.
finding.correction: Verified sound as a structural finding, with one wrong consequence removed. CLAIMED (in difference): 'DR1 holds a separate stored answer per branch, so a user who picks Transit, answers, switches to Transhipment and switches back still sees the transit answers; the frontend's single destinationCountry and portOfExit fields are purged'. TRUE: DR1 purges on flip exactly as the frontend does. Every POST to /reason-for-import writes null to each branch field whose reason is not the one submitted (app/routes.js:10252-10265, and the same nulling in the soft-save branch at :10222-10241), so Transit then Transhipment then Transit loses the transit answers on DR1 too. The frontend's obligation model does the same thing by a different route — purposeInInternalMarket, destinationCountry, portOfExit and exitDate each go out of scope and are purged when the reason moves (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js). If anything the frontend keeps MORE, not less: because one destinationCountry field serves both Transit and Transhipment, a country answered under Transit is still in scope under Transhipment and carries over, where DR1's transhipmentDestinationCountry starts empty. That carry-over is the same per-branch-naming artefact described below, not a DR1 requirement, so it is not raised as its own finding. HOW CHECKED: read every reference to the five branch fields in app/routes.js and the frontend obligation gates. SEPARATELY VERIFIED AND STANDING: the two-destination-country / two-port-of-exit question. DR1 really does render two country selects and two port selects on one page, with identical labels ('Destination country', 'Port of exit'), identical 41-entry and 10-entry lists and identical error text ('Select a destination country', 'Select a port of exit' — app/routes.js:1396-1440), and the review page collapses them to one row per concept keyed on the reason (app/routes.js:4641-4668). Two inputs cannot share a name attribute, so the prefixes are a DOM artefact and raising a field-count finding would have been wrong. The one residue is that DR1's review labels the transit port row 'Exit border control post' and the temporary-admission one 'Port of exit' — a DR1 inconsistency, and a matter for the review slice, not this one. Also verified: reveal order (app/routes.js DOM at the transhipment capture shows transit-exit-border-control-post before transit-destination-country, and temporary-admission-exit-date before temporary-admission-port-of-exit), frontend page order (flow.js:51-55), the exitDetails task row (task-rows.js:34-39) and the six reveal fields in the captured DOM. No content finding has been absorbed into this one and it has not been sharded: the obligation, copy and list findings on the same fields are correctly separate.

relatedTo.why: the hub row exists only because these questions live on pages of their own; this finding is its stated dependency
DR1 enforces the purpose from the reason page, which is only possible once the question is on that page
